column1: Where does the lymphatic drainage of the anal canal below the pectinate line flow?
column2: Inguinal lymph nodes.

column1: What anatomical structures form the boundaries of Hesselbach's triangle?
column2:
Medial: Rectus abdominis lateral border.
Lateral: Inferior epigastric vessels.
Inferior: Inguinal ligament.

column1: What is the common origin of most anorectal abscesses and fistulae?
column2: Infection and obstruction of the anal crypt glands (cryptoglandular hypothesis).

column1: What key structural features must be evaluated when determining the anatomy of an anal fistula?
column2: The internal opening site, external opening site(s), primary track course, secondary extensions, and underlying complicating conditions.

column1: What clinical factors influence the presentation and symptom severity of intestinal obstruction?
column2: The anatomical location, duration, underlying pathology, and presence or absence of intestinal ischemia.

column1: What exception applies to Goodsall's Rule for an anterior external opening located more than $3 \text{ cm}$ from the anal verge?
column2: It curves posteriorly to open in the posterior midline (behaving like a posterior fistula).

column1: What is the characteristic clinical symptom of an acute anal fissure?
column2: Severe, sharp burning pain during and after defecation, often accompanied by bright red blood on toilet paper.

column1: What underlying tissue change forms symptomatic internal hemorrhoids?
column2: Engorgement and displacement of submucosal arteriovenous vascular cushions within the anal canal.

column1: What is an ileostomy?
column2: A planned surgical opening made in the small intestine (ileum) to divert intestinal contents to the abdominal wall.

column1: From which artery do the inferior rectal arteries originate?
column2: Internal pudendal artery.

column1: Why has the use of transverse loop colostomies fallen out of favor?
column2: They are difficult to manage, prone to stomal prolapse, and may compromise the marginal arterial supply to the anastomosis.

column1: What open tension-free repair technique is widely used for inguinal hernia management?
column2: Lichtenstein mesh repair.

column1: How does an appendicular abscess differ clinically from a phlegmonous appendicular mass?
column2: An abscess contains a fluid-filled purulent collection and presents with high fever, chills, and systemic toxicity.

column1: From which major artery does the superior rectal artery originate?
column2: Inferior mesenteric artery.

column1: Which imaging alternatives are acceptable for staging colorectal cancer if spiral CT is unavailable?
column2: Chest X-ray combined with liver ultrasound.

column1: What primary purpose does a temporary loop stoma serve?
column2: It defunctions and protects a distal surgical repair or anastomosis while it heals.

column1: Name four classic symptoms of mechanical intestinal obstruction.
column2: Colicky abdominal pain, vomiting, abdominal distention, and absolute constipation.

column1: What routine traditional intervention has fallen out of favor prior to elective colon cancer surgery?
column2: Mechanical bowel preparation.

column1: According to Goodsall's Rule, what track does an external opening anterior to the transverse anal line follow?
column2: A direct radial path into the anal canal.

column1: Why do femoral hernias carry a significantly higher risk of incarceration and strangulation than inguinal hernias?
column2: The femoral ring has rigid, narrow, and unyielding anatomical borders (such as the lacunar ligament).

column1: Are non-specific anal fistulae more common in men or women?
column2: Men.

column1: Is fever a typical cardinal sign of uncomplicated simple intestinal obstruction?
column2: No; fever is a late feature indicating bowel ischemia, necrosis, or septicemia.

column1: What does the development of peritonism indicate in a patient with intestinal obstruction?
column2: Intestinal ischemia, infarction, or frank bowel perforation.

column1: What is the imaging modality of choice to evaluate suspected appendicular mass or abscess in an obese or diabetic patient?
column2: Contrast-Enhanced Computed Tomography (CECT) of the abdomen and pelvis.

column1: Which vessels supply arterial blood to the anal canal?
column2: Superior, middle, and inferior rectal vessels.

column1: According to Goodsall's Rule, what track does an external opening posterior to the transverse anal line follow?
column2: A curved path entering the anal canal in the posterior midline.

column1: Which type of groin hernia bulges directly forward through Hesselbach's triangle?
column2: Direct inguinal hernia.

column1: A 24-year-old female presents with 5 days of right iliac fossa pain, fever with chills, and a soft $4 \text{ cm} \times 3.5 \text{ cm}$ mass in the RIF. What is the most likely diagnosis?
column2: Appendicular abscess.

column1: What stomal complication is transverse loop colostomy particularly prone to?
column2: Prolapse.

column1: Where does the upper half of the anal canal drain venous blood?
column2: Superior rectal vein into the portal system via the inferior mesenteric vein.

column1: Why does rectal cancer require additional local imaging beyond standard CT staging?
column2: To assess the exact depth of local tumor invasion and mesorectal fascia involvement.

column1: Where does an indirect inguinal hernia enter the anterior abdominal wall?
column2: Through the deep (internal) inguinal ring, lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels.

column1: What anatomic landmark separates indirect from direct inguinal hernias?
column2: Inferior epigastric vessels (indirect hernia is lateral; direct hernia is medial).

column1: Which clinical examination finding strongly suggests an intra-abdominal testicular neoplasm when a male patient presents with an RIF mass?
column2: An empty ipsilateral scrotal sac (undescended testis).

column1: What diagnostic intervention is required following complete aspiration of pus from a tuberculous cervical lymph node swelling?
column2: Fine Needle Aspiration Cytology (FNAC) of the residual nodal swelling.

column1: What non-pharmacological preoperative precaution should be fitted to prevent thromboembolism in colorectal surgery?
column2: Antiembolism stockings.

column1: Which stoma type has largely replaced the transverse loop colostomy for temporary distal protection?
column2: Loop ileostomy.

column1: From which major artery do the middle rectal arteries branch?
column2: Internal iliac artery.

column1: Which imaging technique is used for local staging in rectal cancer?
column2: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) of the pelvis.

column1: What is the standard modality for staging colorectal cancer?
column2: Spiral CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis.

column1: What defines a fistula-in-ano?
column2: A chronic abnormal communication between the anal canal/rectum and perianal skin, lined by granulation tissue.

column1: Which underlying systemic or local conditions can complicate or cause fistula-in-ano?
column2: Crohn's disease, tuberculosis, hidden abscess, or underlying anorectal malignancy.

column1: What is the primary anatomical purpose of Goodsall's Rule?
column2: To predict the course of the primary fistula track and location of the internal opening based on the position of the external opening.

column1: How does severe abdominal distention in intestinal obstruction cause respiratory embarrassment?
column2: Increased intra-abdominal pressure elevates the diaphragm and restricts lung expansion.

column1: A 45-year-old male presents with a non-tender, partly hard/firm RIF mass present for 18 months and an empty right scrotum. What is the diagnosis?
column2: Testicular tumor in an undescended (cryptorchid) intra-abdominal testis.

column1: What is the most common anatomical location of an acute anal fissure?
column2: Posterior midline of the anal canal.

column1: In which anatomical clock positions do primary internal hemorrhoids classically occur?
column2: 3, 7, and 11 o'clock positions (in lithotomy position).

column1: Where does a femoral hernia present relative to the inguinal ligament?
column2: Inferior and lateral to the pubic tubercle, below the inguinal ligament.

column1: How does carcinoma of the caecum typically present compared to an acute appendicular mass?
column2: Caecal carcinoma presents as a slowly progressive, non-tender, hard mass often accompanied by iron-deficiency anemia, without acute inflammatory signs.

column1: Why must hernial orifices be routinely examined in every patient with suspected intestinal obstruction?
column2: To exclude strangulated or incarcerated external abdominal hernias as the underlying cause.

column1: What is a colostomy?
column2: A planned surgical opening in the colon brought to the abdominal wall to divert feces and flatus.

column1: What systemic fluid imbalance arises as a late manifestation of intestinal obstruction?
column2: Severe dehydration leading to oliguria and hypovolemic shock.
